free_text_notes.physician_note: 73-year-old woman with CAD s/p PCI, CKD stage 3, admitted 5/22 with acute decompensated heart failure (EF 30%). Transitioned from IV to oral diuretic yesterday; weight stable.
free_text_notes.nursing_note: Vitals stable this shift. Tolerating diet. 5/27 07:00: CVS reports sacubitril/valsartan needs prior authorization; claim rejected, patient cannot pick it up today. PT recommends assistance with all transfers for now. Patient asked what the new sacubitril/valsartan 24/26 mg twice daily is for; teaching still needed. A venous thromboembolism risk assessment was completed on admission as per standard protocol. The patient received appropriate preventive measures during the stay. These are no longer needed after discharge. Mild swelling was noted in the patient's ankles on examination. This is an expected baseline finding for this condition and is not a new or worsening problem.
